title: hotfix: tighter SLO enforcement + circuit-breaker regional failover and load-shedding
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: A production incident on 2026-02-17 revealed that under a regional hardware degradation we were not shedding load fast enough and our global SLOs (p99 latency, availability) slipped. This hotfix tightens SLO enforcement logic, adjusts circuit breaker thresholds and adds an explicit regional failover path that prefers lower-cost fallback variants when remote capacity is constrained.

Summary of changes: - Reduce the circuit-breaker trip window from 60s -> 30s for latency and increase failure-rate sensitivity for short spikes. - Introduce a soft load-shedding mode: requests are tagged and probabilistically rejected when local capacity is > 95% for > 15s, with clear metrics and counters. - Add regional_failover routing in region_routing.go: when CB trips or capacity > threshold, route traffic to secondary region with capacity check and optional model-variant fallback. - Make SLO enforcement component emit richer events for paging and tie alerts to the new slo_enforcement metrics. - Add integration / canary gating: a canary flag (feature/regional-failover) defaults to enabled for Dedicated customers and is off for hosted until safety window passes.

Checklist: [x] adjust thresholds and windows, [x] add metrics and tracing spans, [x] add unit & integration tests, [x] rerun flaky CI jobs, [x] instrument rollback toggles and feature flag, [x] update runbook links.

Related: Linear ENG-4172, SRE-88. Incident ticket SUP-4421. See doc link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4172/slo-enforcement-hotfix.

Testing: unit tests added for circuit breaker edge cases and load-shedding probability. Integration test simulates regional outage and verifies failover path uses capacity filter and model variant fallback. CI initially had one flaky integration test (test_region_failover_simulation) that failed on first run; re-ran and it passed. Canary rollout performed to dedicated clusters in us-east-1 for one hour with no regression in error budget.

Rollback plan: feature/regional-failover flag can be toggled off via console or infra API; CB threshold change is behind a runtime config and can be reverted without code deploy.

Release notes (summary): Hotfix to improve SLO enforcement under regional degradation: tighter circuit-breaker windows, probabilistic load-shedding to protect p99 latency, and deterministic regional failover path with capacity-aware routing.
commits: fix(runtime): tighten circuit breaker window and failure sensitivity (circuit_breaker.go)
feat(routing): add regional_failover path with capacity checks and model-variant fallback (region_routing.go)
chore(tests): integration test for regional failover and simulation harness updates
review_comments: Marco Reyes (review): Please make sure the probabilistic load-shedding rate is configurable per-customer; we should not hardcode percentages.
Aisha Patel (author): Updated load_shedder to read rate from runtime config and added unit tests for per-customer overrides.
Lin Zhao (review): Suggest adding a histogram of time-to-recover for CB so ops can tune window. Added a tiny change to emit recovery_time_ms metric.
Evelyn Cho (approval): Verified canary in us-east-1 for Dedicated; no regressions observed. Approving for merge after CI green.
SRE note: We observed elevated error budget consumption before the fix; post-deploy graphs show immediate stabilization.
release_notes:
- Hotfix: tighten circuit breaker windows to reduce p99 latency regression under spikes.
- Add probabilistic load-shedding to protect overall availability and latency SLOs.
- Add regional failover path with capacity and model-variant fallback.
- Backwards-safe: runtime configs and feature flag for rollback.
